# Jetpacs applet authoring

## Current project context

```json
!`sh tools/jetpacs-info.sh`
```

The JSON above is the contract and its digest, the installed renderer extensions, the packaged applets and, once a Companion has connected from this Emacs, `last_profile`: what it advertised the last time a session reached READY. Author against `last_profile` when it is present — only its `node_types`, `builtins`, `features` and `extensions` travel to that device — and against the catalog below otherwise. Run `sh tools/jetpacs-info.sh` again after connecting a different device.

## Key concepts

- **One IR.** A builder returns the plist/vector screen IR (`:t` first, wire member names with underscores, children as vectors); the same datum is inspected, gated and serialized. No parallel AST, no codegen.
- **Emacs owns state and policy.** The Companion renders, keeps drafts and delivery records, and dispatches named actions back; it evaluates nothing.
- **Data document.** `jetpacs-ref` binds a member to a pointer; `jetpacs-template` expands rows; `jetpacs-when` predicates on `:visible_when` show or hide keyed children; handlers patch with `jetpacs-app-defer-patch`/`-sync` and refresh only on a shape change.
- **Actions are a durability boundary.** `accepted` means the effect is durable; handlers take `(ARGS PARAMS)` and return `accepted`, `stale` or `rejected`.
- **Negotiated vocabulary.** Every node, builtin, feature and extension must be in the target profile; the shell gates refuse what is not.

## Workflow

1. Read `jetpacs-applet-mcp/APPLET-GUIDE.md` (lifecycle, builders, data document, actions) and `jetpacs-applet-mcp/DETERMINISM.md` (the determinism envelope). With the `jetpacs-applets` MCP running, `jetpacs_applet_guide`, `jetpacs_describe_node`, `jetpacs_node_examples`, `jetpacs_describe_actions` and `jetpacs_catalog` answer the same questions live; after choosing a node, look at its examples before writing it.
2. Scaffold with `jetpacs_applet_template` (or copy `jetpacs-applet-mcp/examples/hello/hello.el`), register the app, its roots and actions.
3. Build screens from the catalog below; bind values, template lists, make parts conditional instead of rebuilding.
4. Validate statically (`jetpacs_validate_applet`), run the applet's ERT suite, byte-compile with warnings as errors into a temporary directory, then a narrow device flow.

## Key exports

| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `jetpacs-defapp` | Register an app with its roots and lifecycle. |
| `jetpacs-chrome-define-root` | Register a chrome app's screen stack root and its `:data-builder`. |
| `jetpacs-shell-define-root` | Register a plain surface root and its `:data-builder`. |
| `jetpacs-defaction` | Register a dotted action handler with `:doc` and `:args`. |
| `jetpacs-action` | Emit a remote ActionDescriptor; builtins have their own constructors. |
| `jetpacs-with-attrs` | Merge universal attributes (`:key`, `:id`, `:visible_when`, …) into a node. |
| `jetpacs-ref` | Bind a member to a JSON Pointer in the surface data document. |
| `jetpacs-when` | One `visible_when` predicate: path, op and operand. |
| `jetpacs-template` | Expand one row node per element of a bound array. |
| `jetpacs-app-defer-refresh` | Re-push a surface after a handler. |
| `jetpacs-app-defer-patch` | Patch the data document after a handler (`jetpacs-data-set`, `-remove`, `-insert`). |
| `jetpacs-app-defer-sync` | Patch a keyed array by diff after a handler. |
| `jetpacs-shell-push` | Push a surface through the sender gates. |

## Nodes (EBP core, 49)

Every core node is built by its `jetpacs-*` constructor; member types are the contract's SPEC 17.1 tags. Examples per node are in `jetpacs-applet-mcp/catalog/CATALOG.md` and the `jetpacs_node_examples` MCP tool.

- text: { text: string, style?: enum[body|title|headline|caption|label|mono], font_weight?: font-weight, color?: color, selectable?: boolean, max_lines?: positive-integer, syntax?: identifier } - A text node showing plain string TEXT (SPEC §17.2). ## Nodes (jetpacs.material3, 5) - Jetpacs' Material 3 design implementation for Jetpacs Compose nodes.

Manifest `renderer-extensions/jetpacs-material3.json`, schema sha256 99105d126640bae463fd4359753903f109ca9cfc68685f5ef7764e9068e27a87. A node travels only to a target whose profile advertises both the node type and the extension.

- material3.assist_chip: { label: text, enabled?: boolean, icon?: identifier, on_tap?: action, variant?: enum[flat|elevated|suggestion|elevated_suggestion] } - A compact Material assist chip with a label, an optional icon and tap action. [targets: app, dialog] [events: on_tap] [elisp: jetpacs-material3-assist-chip (label &key on-tap icon variant enabled)]
  - label: The chip text.
  - icon: A Material icon identifier shown before the label.
  - variant: The chip style.
  - example (m3-catalog, AssistChipSample): `{"icon":"settings","label":"Assist Chip","on_tap":{"action":"m3catalog.demo","args":{"message":"Assist Chip"}},"t":"material3.assist_chip"}`
  - example (m3-catalog, ElevatedAssistChipSample): `{"icon":"settings","label":"Assist Chip","on_tap":{"action":"m3catalog.demo","args":{"message":"Assist Chip"}},"t":"material3.assist_chip","variant":"elevated"}`
- material3.split_button: { on_tap: action, checked?: boolean, enabled?: boolean, icon?: identifier, items?: array<menu-item>(0..64), label?: text, on_change?: action, on_trailing_tap?: action, size?: enum[xsmall|small|medium|large|xlarge], trailing_description?: text, trailing_icon?: identifier, trailing_label?: text, variant?: enum[filled|tonal|elevated|outlined] } - A Material split button: a leading action half and a trailing half that opens items or toggles; checked and on_change make it stateful. [targets: app, dialog] [events: on_tap, on_change, on_trailing_tap] [elisp: jetpacs-material3-split-button (label on-tap &key icon variant size trailing-icon trailing-label trailing-description checked on-change on-trailing-tap items enabled)]
  - on_tap: The leading half's action.
  - checked: The published toggle state when the button is a toggle.
  - items: Menu items the trailing half opens.
  - on_change: Dispatched with the next toggle value injected as args.value.
  - on_trailing_tap: The trailing half's action when it has no items.
  - example (m3-catalog, FilledSplitButtonSample): `{"checked":false,"icon":"edit","id":"split-button-filled","label":"My Button","on_change":{"action":"m3catalog.demo","args":{"message":"Toggle Button"}},"on_tap":{"action":"m3catalog.demo","args":{"message":"My Button"}},"t":"material3.split_button","trailing_description":"Toggle Button","variant":"filled"}`
  - example (m3-catalog, SplitButtonWithUnCheckableTrailingButtonSample): `{"icon":"edit","label":"My Button","on_tap":{"action":"m3catalog.demo","args":{"message":"My Button"}},"on_trailing_tap":{"action":"m3catalog.demo","args":{"message":"Toggle Button"}},"t":"material3.split_button","trailing_description":"Toggle Button","variant":"filled"}`
- material3.app_bar_row: { items: array<bar-item>(1..64), max_items?: integer(1..64), overflow_icon?: identifier } - A horizontal Material app-bar item strip that overflows surplus items into a menu. [targets: app] [elisp: jetpacs-material3-app-bar-row (items &key overflow-icon max-items)]
  - items: The bar items in order.
  - max_items: How many items stay visible before the rest overflow.
  - overflow_icon: The icon of the overflow menu button.

## Actions

Jetpacs action vocabulary (derived from contract.json + platform Elisp)

Remote semantic actions are open-world names. An applet may define any dotted EBP identifier with jetpacs-defaction and emit it with jetpacs-action; the Companion generically dispatches the name and does not need one Kotlin implementation per applet verb.

Remote descriptor required fields: action
Remote descriptor optional fields: args, when_offline, dedupe, ttl_s, confirm, capture_fields, open_surface
Offline policies: drop, queue, wake

Native builtins (10; closed, profile-advertised vocabulary):
- clipboard.copy — required: builtin, text; optional: none; Elisp: jetpacs-clipboard-copy
- companion.settings.open — required: builtin; optional: none; Elisp: jetpacs-settings-open
- dialog.dismiss — required: builtin; optional: none; Elisp: jetpacs-dialog-dismiss
- dialog.submit — required: builtin; optional: value, capture_fields; Elisp: jetpacs-dialog-submit
- share.send — required: builtin, text; optional: title; Elisp: jetpacs-share
- surface.open — required: builtin, surface; optional: none; Elisp: jetpacs-surface-open
- trigger.fire — required: builtin, id; optional: none; Elisp: jetpacs-trigger-fire
- uri.open — required: builtin, uri; optional: none; Elisp: jetpacs-uri-open
- variant.switch — required: builtin, id; optional: value; Elisp: jetpacs-variant-switch
- view.switch — required: builtin, view; optional: none; Elisp: jetpacs-view-switch

Support rule: add ordinary applet behavior by registering an Emacs handler; change EBP/Companion only for a new descriptor field, builtin, node/member, method, capability, or platform integration. Negotiated surface profiles remain authoritative for whether one connected Companion supports a builtin.

## Critical Rules

These rules are always enforced. Each heading links to a file with Incorrect/Correct Elisp pairs.

### IR and builders → [ir.md](./rules/ir.md)

- **Builders are pure readers of explicit state and return the screen IR; effects belong in actions.**
- **Build nodes with the constructors, never as hand-written wire plists.**
- **Children are passed as arguments to a container constructor; the IR is data, not text.**
- **Node ids are unique per document and sibling keys per parent; identity is authored, never generated per render.**

### Data document, templates and conditional nodes → [data.md](./rules/data.md)

- **Bind a value with `jetpacs-ref` and patch it; do not bake it into the node and re-push.**
- **Expand a list with `jetpacs-template` over a bound array; key every row from the item.**
- **Hide a node with `:visible_when` on a keyed child; keep siblings keyed and nothing stateful beneath it.**
- **Patch with `jetpacs-app-defer-patch` or `-sync`; refresh only when the shape changed.**

### Actions and handlers → [actions.md](./rules/actions.md)

- **Action names are dotted EBP identifiers, registered with `jetpacs-defaction` and emitted with `jetpacs-action`; args are plain data.**
- **A handler takes `(ARGS PARAMS)`, makes its effect durable, then returns `accepted`, `stale` or `rejected`; only presentation is deferred.**
- **No blocking call and no prompt inside a dispatch; confirmation belongs on the descriptor, remote work in a durable queue.**
- **Validate with `jetpacs_validate_applet` and the shell gates; never guess a member the catalog does not list.**

### Theme, colors and extensions → [theme.md](./rules/theme.md)

- **Color with a theme role, never a hex literal.**
- **Never author per-mode colors; the role adapts to dark mode.**
- **Derived tokens are not EBP names; use a role, not a Material or design token.**
- **An extension node needs its extension installed and advertised by the target profile; fall back when it is not.**

### Adding applets from a registry → [registry.md](./rules/registry.md)

- **Registry must be explicit: ask which registry when the user does not say; never default to one.**
- **Resolve and dry-run before any install; read the diff of every file that would be overwritten.**
- **Never pass --overwrite, or confirm an overwrite on the device, without the user's explicit approval.**
- **Never fetch or load registry Elisp yourself; the tools verify sha256 and read with a throwaway obarray, and only the App Store's consent gate loads.**
